summary.headline: IG Petrochemicals Q1 FY27 revenue rose 30% to INR625 crore and EBITDA jumped to INR120 crore (19.2% margin) on higher realisations, not volumes.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 30% to INR625 crore, with gross profit about INR207 crore (33% margin) and PAT of INR71 crore, driven by price realisation across products. Volumes were lower, at about 40,000-45,000 tonnes, and sales were 10-15% lower quarter-on-quarter, as export shipments slipped on logistics congestion and some domestic demand moderated in April-May before recovering in June. The plasticizer plant (75,000 tonnes, DOP/DINP/DBP/DIDP) completed mechanical completion in March 2026 and is targeted to start in August or early September 2026. Management guided to about 2 lakh tonnes of phthalic anhydride volume for FY27 (+/-2-3%) and said current spreads of $250-300/t are above the 10-year average of $200-250/t.

financial_highlights.value: INR120 crore (19.2% margin; INR112 crore excluding other income)
financial_highlights.change: vs INR13 crore in Q1 FY26 (margin 2.7%)

financial_highlights.value: INR49 crore; DEP INR28-29 crore, maleic INR17-18 crore
Industry spread $250-300/t; company about $100-120/t above that
financial_highlights.change: Q4 FY26 gross margin stated as 28% (transcript errata)

segments.name: Phthalic anhydride (PAN)
segments.commentary: Volume about 40,000-45,000 t in Q1, 10-15% lower QoQ; price realisation up 30-40% QoQ on feedstock and product prices. Paint (alkyd) sector took 20-25% of PAN quantity; specialty chemicals 4-5%.

segments.name: Plasticizers (new)
segments.commentary: 75,000 t plant with DOP, DINP, DBP, DIDP; start targeted late August or early September 2026 at 1,500-2,000 t initially, then 2,000-3,000 t per month. FY27 balance-year target of 15,000-20,000 t; 50,000-65,000 t in FY28.

segments.name: DEP
segments.commentary: Debottlenecked last quarter; run rate now about 10,000 t per annum vs 6,000-7,000 t earlier; INR28-29 crore revenue in Q1.

segments.name: Maleic anhydride
segments.commentary: INR17-18 crore revenue in Q1, with realisation improved; maleic prices about 20-25% below phthalic due to Chinese oversupply.

segments.name: CBG (Raichur)
segments.commentary: Project progressing; commercial start targeted October-December 2026, negligible FY27 contribution. New national CBG policy raised capital subsidy by 40-50% and CBG prices by 33% for domestic sales (announced the day before the call).

guidance_outlook: FY27 phthalic anhydride volume guided at about 2 lakh tonnes (+/-2-3%) against 2.75 lakh tonnes capacity; medium-term volume target 2.30-2.40 lakh tonnes as utilisation improves and plasticizers ramp.

Plasticizer contribution for balance FY27: about 15,000-20,000 t; at full 75,000 t capacity, management cited gross revenue of about INR1,000 crore and net revenue of INR500-600 crore at current prices.
Quarterly EBITDA: management said next one to two quarters look good, but declined to forecast the full year; if spreads hold at $200-250/t, EBITDA margin is expected at 15-16%.
Interest about INR10 crore annualised and depreciation INR20 crore annualised (about INR5-6 crore per quarter) once plasticizer is commissioned.
Management expects spreads to normalise within 3-6 months if a full US-Iran settlement occurs; no explicit view on spreads otherwise.
Anti-dumping duty on PAN from China ($40/t) and Korea ($140/t) extended for 5 years effective 1 August 2026; management estimated landed import cost 10-15% above current price.
capex_capacity: Plasticizer plant: mechanical completion March 2026; initial capacity 75,000 t; commercial start targeted August/early September 2026; management cited INR180-200 crore invested, asset turnover about 5x, payback about 4 years.
DEP debottlenecking completed in the last quarter; run rate about 10,000 t per annum.
Phthalic anhydride capacity 2.75 lakh t; plant capacity utilisation currently 65-70%, targeted at 80-90% soon.
Operating plants: about 3-3.5 plants running in Q1 (management's wording); 'fifth plant' referenced as part of future steady-state.
Phased switch from LSFO and diesel to natural gas initiated; solar and renewable integration ongoing.
demand_pricing: Q1 demand moderated in April-May as feedstock prices rose 50-60%, hitting plasticizer and specialty chemicals; June saw recovery to near pre-February 2026 levels. Alkyd resin for paints was strong; UPR and CPC stable.
Domestic industry operating at about 60-65% utilisation; imports minimal, so domestic players supply most demand.
Export volumes weak (normally 15-30% of sales) due to container shortages and port congestion at JNPT and Mundra; freight up 30-50% and congestion costs of $80-120/t cited.
Maleic anhydride prices about $1,100/t vs $600-700/t a year earlier per analyst; China added about 2 million t maleic capacity; management described the global market as oversupplied.
Import cost estimate: Chinese/Korean PAN landed about 3-5% above domestic on a like-for-like basis, after freight, duties and ADD.
Management said spread of $250-300/t is above the 10-year average ($200-250/t, later $200-220/t).

qa_highlights.question: What was the industry demand in Q1 and did it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Demand moderated in April and May as feedstock prices rose 50-60%, then recovered to normal by June. Alkyd resin was strong, while specialty chemicals and plasticizers were weaker.

qa_highlights.question: Why was volume only 40,000-45,000 t, and is 5 lakh t still the target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said full-year guidance is 2 lakh t (+/-2-3%), not 5 lakh t. Q1 export volumes were hit by logistics congestion, and some sales slipped into July under delivered terms.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable spread and EBITDA per tonne?
qa_highlights.answer: Current spread is $250-300/t, with the company earning about $100-120/t above market from yield and byproducts. Management said EBITDA margin of about $200-250/t implies a 15-16% EBITDA margin.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plasticizer ramp-up and revenue outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Start at 1,500-2,000 t, then 2,000-3,000 t per month. FY27 balance-year target is 15,000-20,000 t. Full 75,000 t capacity implies net revenue of INR500-600 crore; EBITDA margin of 10-12% and net margin 4-5% were cited.

qa_highlights.question: How do spreads trend if the geopolitical situation eases?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to forecast spreads, but said if there is a full US-Iran settlement, prices could normalise within 3-6 months.

qa_highlights.question: What are the raw material and inventory conditions?
qa_highlights.answer: The company sources 40-50% of ortho-xylene domestically and 40-50% by import, and holds 5,000-10,000 t of inventory (15-20 days). Import lead times have stretched to 40-50 days.

risks_watch: Feedstock and crude volatility: spreads depend on Middle East tensions; management said all petrochemical prices will stay high while crude remains elevated.
Export and logistics disruption: container shortages, port congestion at JNPT and Mundra, and freight costs up 30-50%, plus longer working-capital cycles for imports and exports.
Plasticizer commissioning timing (August-September 2026) and quality approvals; management deferred quality questions to the next one or two quarters.
Chinese oversupply of maleic and PAN; ADD of $40/t (China) and $140/t (Korea) is fixed per tonne and may be small relative to current prices.

Data inconsistencies in the call: volume (40,000-45,000 t vs 46,000-48,000 t), Q4 gross margin (28% per errata vs 32%/73% in the transcript), and the Q4 EBITDA figure (INR67-68 crore raised by analyst). Verify against the filing.
Q1 inventory gain of INR10-15 crore is estimated, not calculated, so underlying EBITDA is uncertain.
summary.management_tone: Confident on margins and the plasticizer launch, but guarded on forward numbers: management declined to forecast full-year EBITDA and spreads, and deferred quality and EBITDA questions on the new plant to later quarters. Commentary on the Middle East and freight disruption was cautious.
key_quotes: So typically, right now, the margin is between $250 to $300, I G is making around $100, $150 -- $120 extra because of the operating efficiency and the byproduct.
I think let's wait rather than commenting on that, let it be reflected in the performance. I would not like to comment about the future.
The facility will have an initial capacity of 75,000 tonnes and expected to start commercial production before September 2026.

growth.why: Management guides plasticizer volumes of 15,000-20,000 t and INR200-250 cr revenue for the balance of FY27 from the 75,000 t plant starting Aug-Sep 2026, with utilisation rising from 65-70% toward 80-90%; PAN volume held at about 2 lakh t (+/-2-3%) and FY28 volume 2.3-2.4 lakh t, but the call gives no full-year revenue growth figure and EBITDA outlook is limited to the next one to two quarters.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management expects EBITDA margin of 15-16% at $200-250/t spreads versus Q1's 19.2% (INR112 crore excluding other income), and the plasticizer plant is guided at 10-12% EBITDA margin, which dilutes the mix.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 75,000 t plasticizer plant completed mechanical completion in March 2026 with commercial start targeted August/early September 2026, initial 1,500-2,000 t then 2,000-3,000 t per month; FY27 balance target 15,000-20,000 t.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Plasticizer volumes of 15,000-20,000 t in the FY27 balance and total FY28 volume of 2.30-2.40 lakh t vs about 2 lakh t PAN in FY27, with utilisation rising from 65-70% toward 80-90%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is 65-70% (target 80-90%), below the 80%+ threshold, and the 75,000 t plasticizer plant is already committed, so a new capex announcement is only possible, not likely; CBG at Raichur is already under construction.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: PAN volume guidance was held at about 2 lakh t (+/-2-3%) against a 2.75 lakh t capacity, and management gave no revenue upgrade; the Q1 19.2% EBITDA margin depends on spreads and an INR10-15 crore inventory gain that is not calculated.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management declined to forecast full-year EBITDA or spreads, and spreads of $250-300/t could normalise within 3-6 months on a US-Iran settlement, with EBITDA margin falling to 15-16% at $200-250/t spreads versus 19.2% in Q1.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Plasticizers (DOP, DINP, DBP, DIDP) start at 1,500-2,000 t initially, then 2,000-3,000 t per month, with a 50,000-65,000 t target in FY28.

rows.label: Anti-dumping duty on PAN from China and Korea extended 5 years
rows.why: ADD of $40/t (China) and $140/t (Korea) extended for 5 years, and management estimates landed import cost 10-15% above current price, which supports domestic pricing.

rows.label: CBG plant at Raichur commercial start
rows.why: Project progressing with commercial start targeted Oct-Dec 2026, negligible FY27 contribution, and a national CBG policy raised the capital subsidy by 40-50% and CBG prices by 33% for domestic sales.

rows.label: Import and export logistics delays
rows.why: Export volumes are normally 15-30% of sales but are weak on container shortages and port congestion at JNPT and Mundra, with freight up 30-50% and congestion costs of $80-120/t, and import lead times stretched to 40-50 days.

tone.note: Management was confident on the margin run-rate and the plasticizer launch but declined to forecast full-year EBITDA or spreads and deferred plasticizer quality questions; analysts pressed on the sustainable spread, volume targets versus the 5 lakh t figure, and the Q4 data inconsistencies.
